summary: A Sporting News guide to online MLB betting that profiles six sportsbooks and their baseball offerings. It explains how to use a betting app, live betting, core bet types (moneyline, run line, totals, First 5 Innings), props and futures, line shopping, and common sportsbook rules for baseball wagers.
one_line: Guide to the best 2023 MLB sportsbooks and apps, covering bet types, live betting, props, futures, line shopping and baseball betting rules.
key_facts: The guide profiles DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM, Caesars, Bet365 and BetRivers as MLB betting sites and apps, though it introduces them as 'four favorite' sites.
DraftKings offers MLB prop bets such as First Inning Winner or First Team to Score, plus futures on division winners and the next World Series champion.
Caesars has a cash-out option that lets bettors settle bets early to guarantee a payout, though at a reduced amount.
Bet365 posts daily MLB odds boosts and has a live-betting feature allowing real-time bets on MLB games.
BetRivers' iRush Rewards program lets bettors earn points redeemable for VIP gifts, MLB event tickets, BetRivers branded merchandise and special offers.
A moneyline bet is on which team wins outright; the underdog is shown with a positive (+) number and the favorite with a negative (-) number.
The MLB run line gives the underdog a 1.5-run handicap: the underdog must lose by one run or win outright, while the favorite must win by two runs or more to cover.
Totals bets (over/unders) concern the combined runs of both teams, and the actual winner of the game doesn't matter.
First 5 Innings (F5) bets cover only the first five innings, which often removes the uncertainty of relief pitchers replacing starters.
Popular MLB futures include World Series champion, MVP, home run leader and regular-season win totals.
'Line shopping' means comparing odds across several sportsbooks to find the best price and maximize potential return.
F5 bets are usually actionable after five innings, or 4.5 innings if the home team leads.
For the run line to have action, the game must go 9 innings, or 8½ if the home team is winning.
Player prop wagers only have action if the player is in the starting lineup, and bets can only be placed within the lines of a state with legal online sports betting.
